title: Signs
text:
Everything makes love with silence.

I had been promised a silence like fire, a house of silence.

Suddenly the temple is a circus and the light a drum.
editorial_note: Silence remains lover, fire, and dwelling before the promised sanctuary abruptly becomes spectacle and percussion.

title: Tomorrow…
text:
Tomorrow

they will dress me in ashes at dawn,

they will fill my mouth with flowers.

I shall learn to sleep

in the memory of a wall,

in the breathing of an animal that dreams.
editorial_note: The anticipated burial passes from ash and flowers into an apprenticeship in sleep, housed within wall-memory and an animal’s dream-breath.

title: When You Look at Me…
text:
When you look at me

my eyes are keys,

the wall has secrets,

my fear words, poems.

Only you make of my memory

an entranced traveler,

an unceasing fire.
editorial_note: The omitted verb in my fear words, poems is retained; the beloved’s gaze turns memory into both fascinated motion and inexhaustible flame.

title: In the Clenched Hand of a Dead Man…
text:
In the clenched hand of a dead man,

in the memory of a madman,

in the sorrow of a child,

in the hand reaching for the glass,

in the unreachable glass,

in the thirst as ever.
editorial_note: The repeated in carries each enclosure toward the unreachable vessel; sed de siempre becomes thirst as ever, both perpetual and intimately familiar.

text:
Only thirst

silence

no encounter


beware of me my love

beware of the silent woman in the desert

of the traveler with the empty glass

and of the shadow of her shadow
editorial_note: The warning remains unpunctuated and turns the speaker into three receding figures: silent woman, empty-handed traveler, and doubled shadow.

text:
Life, my life, let yourself fall, let yourself ache, my life,

let yourself be entwined with fire, with innocent silence, with

green stones in the house of night, let yourself

fall and ache, my life.
editorial_note: Déjate doler becomes let yourself ache, preserving both surrender and embodied pain; the long imperative coils through fire, silence, stone, and night.

title: The Splendid Paper Palace of Childhood Pilgrimages…
text:
The splendid paper palace of childhood pilgrimages.


At sunset they will put the tightrope walker in a cage, carry her to a ruined temple, and leave her there alone.
editorial_note: Volatinera becomes the female tightrope walker, preserving precarious performance before the abrupt ritual of caging, ruin, and abandonment.

title: Only
text:
now I understand the truth


it bursts in my desires


and in my misfortunes

in my failed encounters

in my imbalances

in my deliriums


now I understand the truth


now

to go in search of life
editorial_note: Truth is not stated but located in desire, disaster, disjunction, and delirium; the final infinitive leaves the search for life just beginning.
